title: Defeat Has Hardened Trump. It Is Not Good News for Mexico. Fasten Your Seatbelts.
author: SinEmbargo Staff
content:
_This article by SinEmbargo Staff originally appeared in the[November 7, 2026
edition of SinEmbargo](https://www.sinembargo.mx/4900418/la-derrota-endurecio-
a-trump-no-es-buena-noticia-para-mexico-amarrense-el-cinturon/), an
independent Mexican digital news outlet._

**Mexico City, November 7 (SinEmbargo).—** The **President** of the [**United
States**](https://www.sinembargo.mx/tag/estados-unidos/), [**Donald
Trump**](https://www.sinembargo.mx/tag/donald-trump/), has hardened with his
**defeat**. He has elevated someone just like him, or worse, to levels where
he can make even harsher decisions on, for example, **migration** and
**organized crime** , issues on which he can affect **Mexico**.

On Friday, Trump removed his former close adviser, **Susie Wiles** , from the
post of **chief of staff** of the [**White
House**](https://www.whitehouse.gov/), and replaced her with **Stephen
Miller** , his deputy chief of staff. More than any other senior adviser,
Miller pushed for an aggressive use of executive power when Trump returned to
office.

> _The New Yorker_ magazine states bluntly: “Miller has long been one of
> Trump’s most influential advisers. He is, principally, the architect of the
> Administration’s immigration policies, which include violent ICE operations,
> an executive order to end birthright citizenship, the dismantling of the
> legal immigration system, the mass detention of tens of thousands of people
> with no criminal records, and flagrant contempt for court orders.”

> We need a moratorium on immigration from Third World countries until we can
> heal as a nation.
>
> Stephen Miller, last December

Miller said this last December. For him, “healing” has largely consisted of
making the country look more like him. He seems to regard immigrants and his
political opponents as declared enemies.

![Stephen Miller](https://mexicosolidarity.com/wp-
content/uploads/2026/11/02-miller.jpg)“Stephen Miller has long been one of
Trump’s most influential advisers,” according to _The New Yorker_ magazine.
Photo: White House

_The New York Times_ says this morning: “Miller has been the driving force
behind the President’s most forceful actions, including the use of
increasingly hostile tactics to capture immigrants across the country and the
bombing of small boats in the Caribbean Sea and the eastern Pacific Ocean,
which he and Trump declared constituted a foreign invasion.”

> “The President’s choice sent a clear signal about the stance he intends to
> take in his final two years in office and about how little he plans to
> change his approach after the most resounding political defeat in half a
> century. It also put in the spotlight a figure who had already been a key
> target for Democrats, who were looking to use their new powers in Congress
> to rein in the government,” it adds.

Even though it is an outlet sympathetic to Trump, _The Wall Street Journal_
says that Miller, “a shrewd political strategist who has been at Trump’s side
for more than a decade, has been a staunch advocate of the no-limits style of
governing that thrilled the President’s most ardent followers, the MAGA
faithful, and that was repudiated by much of the rest of the country on
Election Day. He succeeds Susie Wiles, who was seen as a moderating force on a
sometimes impulsive President.”

_The Atlantic_ details that while Wiles acted as a kind of counterweight
—making sure Trump was fully informed and understood the risks and
difficulties of any decision—, Miller has acted as an accelerator for a
President who already has impulsive tendencies.

> “One issue on which Wiles and Miller appear to diverge is how to force
> journalists to reveal their sources in the government. Trump has pressured
> the Justice Department to open criminal investigations into leaks on
> national security grounds, and there have been conversations in the White
> House and the Justice Department about various tactics they could employ
> —including arrests— as part of those efforts, according to three people
> familiar with the matter,” the magazine says.

Two of those people told _The Atlantic_ that Wiles had opposed it. “Miller,
however, was in favor and insisted that journalists would soon reveal their
sources, we were told. A Justice Department spokesperson told us by text
message that ‘this is absolutely false,’ but declined to elaborate. A White
House spokesperson told us in a statement that unauthorized leaks ‘will NEVER
be tolerated’ and that those responsible ‘must be held accountable.’”

“Many observers have compared Miller to a kind of Prime Minister in the
current administration,” _The New Yorker_ magazine maintains. “Miller, who has
served as the President’s National Security adviser and foreign policy chief,
has directed many of the government’s most radical actions. This goes far
beyond immigration policy. **The military bombing of alleged drug-trafficking
boats in the Caribbean and the Pacific traces back to Miller**.”

> “The results of the midterm elections forcefully demonstrated public
> opposition to Trump and his policies, and Democrats will now control both
> chambers of Congress by wide margins. However, the President still retains
> immense power, especially in matters of immigration and foreign policy. His
> new chief of staff may well show us how ugly and painful the final stage of
> Trumpism can be,” the publication concludes.

![Donald Trump in the Oval Office](https://mexicosolidarity.com/wp-
content/uploads/2026/11/03-trump.jpg)“The President’s choice of his new chief
of staff sent a clear signal about the stance he intends to take in his final
two years in office,” warned _The New York Times_. Photo: White House
